blocks.text: A1-19 · Cases (iʿrāb): nominative, accusative, genitive
Lesson overview

From A1-01 read the final vowels of the words: -u in ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ , -i ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ -a in ⁧أَقْرَأُ الجَرِيدَةَ⁩ . It's the case endings, and the system that rules is called iʿrāb ( ⁧إِعْرَاب⁩ ). In this unit, you collect what you have seen in a single picture, unity by unity: three cases, their functions, the forms in the different types of names, and two new words that govern them, ⁧كَانَ⁩ and ⁧إِنَّ⁩ . You'll also learn to read a text with all sorts of endings, like a radio journalist, and to recognize cases in unvocal texts. Two weeks; close the form A1.4.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 43–44 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-19), voice synthesis scripts, vocalized texts from previous units, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. appoint the three cases and their basic functions;
2. write and read the endings in singular, dual and plural names, including diptotes and defects;
3. explain why a word has -u, -a or -i in a phrase you know;
4. recognize the effect of ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , ⁧أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ ;
5. read a vocalized text of 120 words both with complete and paused terminations;
6. recognize the traces of cases in texts without vowels.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: What to notice. In ⁧سَأَلَ الصَّحَفِيَّ الوَزِيرُ⁩ the order is verb : object is subject: it is desinence, not position, to say who acts. Without vowels the sentence ( ⁧سأل الصحفي الوزير⁩ ) would be read in the normal order, the journalist asked the minister: in the texts not vocally spoken the verb order is subject by far the most frequent, and it is taken for granted except contrary clues. ⁧اِسْمَعْ⁩ "Listen!" is an imperative (A2). ⁧الحَرَكَات⁩ It's short vowels.
1. What are the cases
An Arabic name changes the final vowel according to its function in the sentence. There are three cases:
Genitive ⁧مَجْرُور⁩ maǧrūr -i · -in ⁧ٍـ⁩ · ⁧ِـ⁩

Because they exist. In Latin and German the cases allow you to move words without losing sense; in Arabic is the same. In the modern spoken language, desinences have almost disappeared and the order of words has become more fixed; Standard Arabic keeps them in vocalized spelling and formal reading. Three reading levels. 1) Pause: no endings at the end of the sentence, which is how you have read the transliteration so far. 2) Complete: all endings except the last before the break (notes, official speeches, Koran). 3) Mixed: the most widespread in the educated speech, with desinences at the points where they serve to ligament or sense. In A1 we ask you to understand the full reading and at least produce the mixed one.

The arrangements. Adjective, affixing and names coordinated with ⁧وَ⁩ take the case of the name to which they refer: ⁧فِي⁩
⁧البَيْتِ⁩ ⁧الكَبِيرِ⁩ , ⁧زَارَ أُخْتَهُ⁩ ⁧وَأَخَاهُ⁩ .
3. Name and accusation in the sentence
. ⁧صَبَاحًارَجَعَ الطَّالِبُ صَبَاحًا⁩ Time supplement (apartment)

A question for every word. To decide desinence ask yourself: is it subject or preached? (nominative) It is object, preached by ⁧كَانَ⁩ / ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ , subject of ⁧إِنَّ⁩ , time, place or way? It comes after a preposition or is the second term of an 'iḍāfa? (genit)
4. The genitive

The genitive has only two functions, but very frequent: after preposition ( ⁧فِي، مِنْ، إِلَى، عَلَى، مَعَ، عِنْدَ، بِـ، لِـ، عَنْ، أَمَامَ⁩ ...) and as the second term of theiḍāfa . In a chain all the terms from the second onwards are to the genitive: ⁧مَكْتَبُ مُدِيرِ⁩ ⁧الشُّرْطَةِ⁩ . A name can be together first term of aiḍāfa is governed by a preposition: ⁧فِي⁩ ⁧مَكْتَبِ⁩ ⁧المُدِيرِ⁩ (genitive for ⁧فِي⁩ , and in turn holds ⁧المُدِيرِ⁩ ).

blocks.text: What to remember. 1) Two forms of male and healthy plural are named and all the rest are given. 2) Female healthy plural: the accusative is equal to the genitive (-āti/-ātin). 3) Diptoths: nothing tanwīn; the indeterminate genitive is -a; with the article or iḍāfa return regular ( ⁧فِي المَدَارِسِ⁩ ). 4) Many words do not show the case: in those cases the function is deduced from the position.
6. ⁧كَانَ⁩ , ⁧إِنَّ⁩ and their sisters

⁧كَانَ⁩ It was, was.A1-18) e ⁧لَيْسَ⁩ ( A1-16) leave the subject to the name and put the predicate to the accused: ⁧كَانَ الجَوُّ⁩ ⁧بَارِدًا⁩ The weather was cold. ⁧كَانَتِ الشَّقَّةُ⁩ ⁧صَغِيرَةً⁩ The apartment was small. ⁧كَانُوا⁩ ⁧مَشْغُولِينَ⁩ They were busy. ⁧إِنَّ⁩ In truth, it certainly opens a nominal sentence and puts the subject to the accusative; the predicate remains at the name: ⁧إِنَّ⁩ ⁧الجَوَّ⁩ ⁧بَارِدٌ⁩ The weather is (just) cold. It is very frequent at the beginning of sentences in formal texts and after ⁧قَالَ⁩ : ⁧قَالَ الوَزِيرُ إِنَّ⁩ ⁧الوَضْعَ⁩ ⁧هَادِئٌ⁩ The Minister said that the situation was calm. Sisters ⁧إِنَّ⁩ they work in the same way: ⁧أَنَّ⁩ ( ⁧أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ⁩ ⁧الدَّرْسَ⁩ ⁧صَعْبٌ⁩ I know that the lesson is difficult, ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ • because it is not ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ ⁧الطُّلَّابَ⁩ ⁧كَثِيرُونَ⁩ ), ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ • but • ⁧لٰكِنَّ⁩ ⁧العَمَلَ⁩ ⁧مُهِمٌّ⁩ ). With a pronoun you attack the suffixes: ⁧إِنَّهُ⁩ , ⁧لِأَنَّهَا⁩ , ⁧لٰكِنَّنِي⁩ ( -nī), ⁧أَنَّهُمْ⁩ . For now, recognize them. In A2 you will use ⁧كَانَ⁩ in all forms and constructions with ⁧أَنَّ⁩ and ⁧أَنْ⁩ .
7. Cases in texts without vowels
Without vowels the endings -u, -a, -disappear. Some traces remain visible:

rows: indeterminate accusation: object, predicate of ⁧كان⁩ / ⁧ليس⁩ , adverb

blocks.text: hamza on ⁧و⁩ / ⁧ا⁩ / ⁧ي⁩ in plurals / ⁧زملاءنا⁩ / ⁧زملاؤنا⁩ name / accusative / genitive in -āʾ ⁧زملائنا⁩

Reading strategy. Look first for the verb, then the subject immediately afterwards; Use these tracks to verify. When the text is ambiguous and the traces are missing, it points to ambiguity: it is a professional competence, not a weakness.
8. Pronunciation

The reading is complete. Read with all desinences, linking them to the following words: al-baytu l-kabīru ǧamīlun ǧiddan . Just stop at the end of the sentence. The tanwīn in front of an alif waṣla. -an , -an , -in followed by an article or by an alif waṣla They take one support: ǧiddani l-yawm (A1-03), muzdaḥimuni l-yawm (A1-04), ʿindahumu ǧtimāʿun (A1-12). -ūna / -īna, -āni / -ayni. It is the desinences that are also felt in reading \"mista": don't leave them out.
9. New lexicon

rows: pf. ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ · ⁧يَسْأَلُ عَنْ⁩ • ask for a change of name

blocks.text: ⁧مُذِيع⁩ muḏīʿ speaker, announcer ⁧ذ ي ع⁩ name pl. ⁧مُذِيعُون⁩
⁧أَهَمّ⁩ most important ahamm ⁧ه م م⁩ adjective . (comparative)

Notes of use. The seasons are used with ⁧فِي⁩ : ⁧فِي الصَّيْفِ⁩ In the summer, it's gonna be fine. ⁧عَزِيزِي⁩ / ⁧عَزِيزَتِي⁩ • expensive / dear • open informal letters. ⁧أَهَمّ⁩ is the comparison of ⁧مُهِمّ⁩ : Comparatives are in A2. ⁧مَرْضَى⁩ is a plural over particular (schema faʿlā), used for sick, injured and prisoners: you will find him in the news.

: ⁧فِي صَفِّي طُلَّابٌ مِنْ بِلَادٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ⁩ . ⁧المَاضِي طَوِيلًا وَصَعْبًا، لِأَنَّ الطُّلَّابَ كَثِيرُونَ هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ⁩
